title: Distance is area
hook: You know the speed at every moment but not the position. Can you still find the distance?

knows: distance = speed x time when the speed is steady
reading a straight-line graph; slope as a rate
doesNotKnow: that total distance is the area under the speed-time graph

misconception: To find distance you need a formula that mentions position; speed alone is not enough when it changes.
objective: The learner can explain that slicing time into strips turns a changing speed into many small speed x time pieces, and that their total approaches the area under the speed line (100 m here).

claims.text: A car speeding up steadily from 0 to 20 m/s over 10 s travels 100 m: the triangle under the speed line, 1/2 x 10 x 20, or the average speed 10 m/s for 10 s.
claims.source: Constant acceleration a = 2 m/s^2: distance = 1/2 a t^2 = 1/2 x 2 x 100 = 100 m; also the area of the triangle; recomputed with node. Idealised model (steady acceleration from rest), labelled on the stage.

claims.text: Strips using the speed at the end of each slice give 200 m with 1 strip, 110 m with 10 and 105 m with 20: always above 100 m and closing in on it. The reveal quotes only the strip counts the learner tried.
claims.source: Right Riemann sum for v = 2t on [0, 10] with n strips = 100 (n + 1) / n; n = 1: 200, 10: 110, 20: 105; the stage computes the bars with the same function; recomputed with node. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): Own node right sums for v = 2t on [0,10]: n=1 200, n=10 110, n=20 105 = 100(n+1)/n > 100; rightSum in Demo.tsx is the same function; reveal quotes seen.lo and seen.hi.

claims.text: Distance travelled is the area under the speed-time graph.
claims.source: Distance = integral of speed over time (for speed >= 0), the fundamental theorem of calculus; e.g. Stewart, Calculus, sec. 5.1 (the distance problem).

claims.text: Each strip is speed times a short time, which is metres: a small distance. Adding strips adds distances.
claims.source: Units: m/s x s = m. The stage's first-strip caption (speed x time = metres) and the 'Strips add up to' readout show it. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): Units m/s x s = m; reveal text lines 54-55 match.

recall.question: A cyclist slows steadily from 8 m/s to 0 over 6 s. Which picture gives the distance she covers?
options: The area of the triangle under her speed line: 1/2 x 6 x 8 = 24 m
Her top speed times the time: 8 x 6 = 48 m
The slope of her speed line
recall.why: Distance is the area under the speed-time graph. A steady slowdown makes a triangle, half of the 48 m rectangle.
